full_judgment: 4. The predecessor of the defendants Nos. 2-6 contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case in short is that the first schedule land belonged to Aftabur Reja Chowdhury, who settled the same with the defendant No.1 on accepting a registered kabuliyat dated 1st December, 1930. Defendant No. 1 has been possessing the northern half. Abut Hashem thereupon sold his share to the defendant No.1 by a registered deed dated 16th November, 1948. The 2nd schedule land belonged to Rajob Ali who died leaving mother, the defendant No.6 and sister Lumar Ma, who subsequently relinquished her interest in favour of Sajida Beanu, the mother of defendant No.6 Sajida Banu died leaving behind the defendant Nos.1-6. Hurmot Ali initially erected two huts on the said land as license and subsequently the defendant No.1 took possession thereof from Hurmot Ali. The plaintiffs created the deeds in collusion with Hurmot Ali in respect of the second schedule land. The Revenue Staffs used to reside in the garden (Baganbari) of the daughter of Aftabur Raju who in collusion with the plaintiffs created the false record. The defendants are in possession of the suit land and they have not dispossessed by the plaintiffs as claimed.
